title: Organic waste
guidance: Food scraps and other biodegradable kitchen waste should generally be kept separate from dry recyclables. Where a wet-waste or composting stream exists, use that stream according to local rules.

title: Paper and cardboard
guidance: Keep paper and cardboard clean and dry for recycling where accepted. Remove obvious food contamination and flatten large cardboard pieces.

title: Plastic packaging
guidance: Check whether the local dry-waste system accepts the specific plastic. Empty containers and keep recyclable material as clean as practical. Avoid assuming every plastic item is recyclable.

title: Glass items
guidance: Use a designated glass/recycling stream where available. Broken glass requires careful handling and may have special collection instructions.

title: Metal containers
guidance: Metal cans and similar recyclable containers can generally enter a dry/recycling stream where accepted. Empty containers before disposal.

title: Electronic waste
guidance: Phones, chargers, computers and other electronic equipment should be taken to an authorized e-waste collection or recycling channel rather than ordinary household bins.

title: Batteries
guidance: Batteries should not be mixed with ordinary household waste. Use an appropriate battery or e-waste collection point and follow local safety instructions.

title: Hazardous and medical waste
guidance: Sharps, medical materials, chemicals and other hazardous items require dedicated handling. Do not mix them with ordinary household waste; follow authorized collection instructions.
